I will keep the farm simple and low-risk. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, where the normal pattern is winter wheat followed by summer maize, and most rain comes in the maize season while wheat usually needs more irrigation. That fits how I would farm at 71: I know this system, I can manage it with ordinary machinery, and it gives me steady grain without the labor pressure of vegetables or other cash crops. Because you did not give a farm size, I will make a concrete decision for **20 mu** of ordinary field land. I will use the whole 20 mu in a wheat-maize rotation. For wheat, I will use an improved common variety instead of chasing high-risk extremes, put fertilizer mainly as base fertilizer plus one topdressing, irrigate about three times if water is available, and keep pesticide use moderate. For summer maize, I will switch to hybrid seed, use less irrigation because summer rain usually does more of the work, and I will simplify field work by rotary tillage after wheat harvest. I am not putting land into vegetables or cotton because, at my age, I would rather protect labor, keep management straightforward, and aim for a stable harvest rather than a more complicated crop mix.
